title: Office Furniture Budget Newcastle: Planning for 10, 20 or 40 Staff
metaTitle: Office Furniture Budget Newcastle: 10–40 Staff | YOS
metaDescription: Plan an office furniture budget in Newcastle, NSW for 10, 20 or 40 staff. Scope workstations, shared spaces, delivery and installation before requesting quotes.
excerpt: Build a Newcastle office furniture budget around the desks you actually need, shared spaces and the installed scope. Use a clearly labelled calculation example and a checklist for supplier quotes.
body:
An office furniture budget in Newcastle should cover the required workstations, meeting and shared furniture, storage, delivery and installation. Staff count helps define the brief, but the actual number of desks and the building access requirements determine what suppliers need to quote. There is no reliable single price per employee without a specification.

This guide helps Newcastle and Hunter business owners prepare a furniture-only budget for teams of 10, 20 or 40. Construction, building services and other FitOut work need separate scopes. The calculation below demonstrates the method; it is not a Newcastle market price guide or a YOS quotation.

## How do you calculate an office furniture budget?

Start with the cost of each specified setting multiplied by its quantity. Add shared furniture and the site-specific delivery and installation scope. Include separately priced accessories, retained furniture handling and any required trade work. Record GST consistently and keep unresolved costs visible.

Use actual supplier quotes to turn that calculation into an approval budget. A catalogue desk price alone does not establish what it costs to set up a usable office.

## Decide how many desks the business needs

Headcount and workstation count are not always the same. A 20-person hybrid team may have a different requirement from a 20-person team attending every day. Start with realistic peak attendance, role requirements, shared-desk arrangements and planned growth.

Do not use average attendance to justify a layout that cannot support a busy day. Test how the space handles visitors, meetings, storage and equipment alongside the desk count.

| Team size | Question to resolve before pricing | Shared spaces to include in the brief |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 staff | Does everyone need an assigned desk, and is growth likely? | Meeting setting, visitor seating and practical storage |
| 20 staff | Which roles need dedicated settings, and what is peak attendance? | Meeting capacity, shared storage, lockers if needed and breakout settings |
| 40 staff | Are teams co-located, rotating attendance or working across zones? | Multiple meeting settings, collaboration areas and a coordinated storage plan |

These are briefing prompts, not prescribed space standards or mandatory furniture lists.

## A calculation example for 10, 20 and 40 workstations

For this fictional arithmetic example only, assume a workstation furniture package costs $1,000, shared furniture costs $3,000 and delivery plus installation costs $2,000. All amounts below exclude GST. These deliberately simple assumptions are not observed supplier rates, Newcastle averages or recommended budget allowances. Replace them with your quoted figures.

| Calculation | 10 workstations | 20 workstations | 40 workstations |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Workstation packages at the assumed $1,000 each | $10,000 | $20,000 | $40,000 |
| Assumed shared furniture | $3,000 | $3,000 | $3,000 |
| Assumed delivery and installation | $2,000 | $2,000 | $2,000 |
| Illustrative total excluding GST | $15,000 | $25,000 | $45,000 |

Holding shared furniture and installation costs constant isolates the workstation calculation. It does not predict a real project: a larger team may need more meeting furniture, additional storage, staged delivery and a different installation scope. Product selection, access and customisation can change every figure.

Before relying on a total, replace each assumption with a specified package and a site-specific quote. Add any unresolved costs, identify exclusions and confirm the GST-inclusive amount where applicable.

## What changes the furniture price in Newcastle?

Product specification is one part of the answer. Compare fixed and height-adjustable desks, seating requirements, screens, monitor arms, storage and finishes against the people using the workplace. A low-cost item that fails the brief is not a saving.

The delivery destination also matters. For a Newcastle CBD office, ask building management about loading access, lift dimensions, permitted delivery times and floor protection. For premises in Wickham, Hamilton, Charlestown or elsewhere in the Hunter, confirm the actual access route and building rules rather than assuming they are simpler.

These locations are planning examples, not claims that all buildings share the same restrictions. Send the complete address and access information to suppliers so delivery costs reflect the site.

## Keep furniture costs separate from building work

Furniture-only procurement can include selection, supply, delivery and assembly. A wider FitOut may also include partitions, lighting, flooring, electrical changes, data work and other services.

Record those workstreams separately so a furniture budget is not mistaken for a complete office project cost. Ask the appropriate professionals to confirm any approval or trade requirements for the proposed changes.

## Reuse and phasing can change the budget

Inventory existing furniture before assuming everything must be replaced. Include dimensions, condition and dismantling requirements, then test retained items against the proposed plan. Allow for moving and reinstallation costs rather than treating reuse as free.

If purchasing in stages, price the whole sequence. Multiple delivery visits, inconsistent finishes or unavailable matching components can undermine an apparently cheaper first stage. Confirm current availability and keep future supply assumptions explicit.

[Audit existing office furniture before moving](/blog/office-furniture-reuse-audit-newcastle)

## Furniture only or a complete office fitout?

Furniture supply and installation is one part of a workplace project. For partitions, building services, consultant inputs, approvals and construction, use our [commercial office fitout budget guide](/blog/commercial-fitout-cost-newcastle-2026) and [client-side office FitOut project management service](/office-fitout). Record these separate scopes before approving the total.

## Prepare a Newcastle furniture quote brief

Give suppliers the same measured plan, desk quantity, furniture schedule, access information and installation scope. Include what you intend to retain and the operating date you are working towards.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much should a Newcastle office allow per staff member?

Use staff count to develop the brief, then price the actual settings and shared spaces. A single per-person allowance can hide differences in desk use, product specification and installation. The example above is a calculation demonstration, not a local price benchmark.

### Does a furniture package include installation?

Only if the proposal says so. Confirm delivery, assembly, placement, packaging removal and access assumptions in writing.

### Can we use a furniture budget as our complete FitOut budget?

No. Building work and specialist services require separate scopes and costs. Check what the project includes before approving the total.

### Can YOS help with a small Newcastle office as well as a larger package?

YOS assesses furniture requirements around the brief, quantities, location, budget and program. Send your plan and requirements so the appropriate scope can be confirmed.
